10744.correction: The lesson explores the concepts of 'accurate' and 'estimate' using simple apparatus to estimate the vital capacity of the lungs.

7163.statement: Pupils often refer to the walls of the alveoli as "cell walls".
7163.correction: This lesson makes the scale of different parts of the gas exchange system clear (e.g. whether a structure is a tissue or cell).

10269.belief: Only animals respire, and that plants only photosynthesise (and do not respire).
10269.statement: Thinking that only animals respire, and that plants only photosynthesise (and do not respire).
10269.correction: This lesson uses examples of plants respiring in order to address this misconception.

177.belief: Aerobic cellular respiration is a single chemical reaction.
177.statement: Aerobic cellular respiration is a single chemical reaction.
177.correction: This lesson uses the terms 'chemical process' and 'series of chemical reactions'.

4066.belief: Learners often assume there is only one type of cellular respiration (aerobic).
4066.statement: Learners often assume there is only one type of cellular respiration (aerobic).
4066.correction: This lesson explores aerobic and anaerobic cellular respiration in humans.

9715.statement: Students can often confuse the word summaries for the different types of cellular respiration.
9715.correction: This lesson directly compares the different word summaries for anaerobic cellular respiration to help understand the differences between them.

5566.belief: Plants take in food from their surroundings.
5566.statement: Plants take in food from their surroundings.
5566.correction: This lesson explores why the things taken in by plants are not food, and the idea that plants make the food they need to survive.

4144.belief: Light is a chemical reactant in photosynthesis and it is turned into food.
4144.statement: Light is a chemical reactant in photosynthesis and it is turned into food.
4144.correction: Challenge the misconception that light is a chemical reactant in photosynthesis.

350.belief: Not appreciating the links between form and function in biological structures.
350.statement: Not appreciating the links between form and function in biological structures.
350.correction: This lesson develops a key cross-cutting idea in biology: the shapes and forms of biological structures are adapted for specific functions.

9679.belief: Most students will be aware that bones can become fossilised but not realise that other remains such as wood or footprints can also become fossils too.
9679.statement: Most students will be aware that bones can become fossilised but not realise that other remains such as wood or footprints can also become fossils too.
9679.correction: This lesson contains a broad range of examples of the types of remains that can become fossilised.

9802.statement: Students struggle to comprehend absolute ages of key events in the history of Earth and evolutionary history.
9802.correction: This lesson provides many examples and context to give students a sense of the differences in time scales involved in the history of Earth and evolution.

9811.belief: As students struggle to remember that plants are alive, they don't think of plants as being adapted to their surroundings.
9811.statement: As students struggle to remember that plants are alive, they don't think of plants as being adapted to their surroundings.
9811.correction: This lesson gives many examples of the adaptations plants have which help them to thrive in their environments.

4417.belief: Many learners think that the only way animals compete for resources is through physical aggression.
4417.statement: Many learners think that the only way animals compete for resources is through physical aggression.
4417.correction: This lessons contains many examples of how animals and other organisms compete for resources.

1816.belief: It is common for students to believe that all types of variation can be passed on from parents to their offspring.
1816.statement: It is common for students to believe that all types of variation can be passed on from parents to their offspring.
1816.correction: This lesson explores examples of variation that can and cannot be passed on from parents to their offspring, and links this to their causes.

9820.belief: Advantageous traits are due to an organism choosing to change itself in order to be successful.
9820.statement: Students often think that advantageous traits are due to an organism choosing to change itself in order to be successful.
9820.correction: This lesson uses CfUs in order to explore and deconstruct this misconception.

10300.belief: Populations of organisms stay the same forever.
10300.statement: Thinking that populations of organisms stay the same forever.
10300.correction: This model clearly demonstrates that populations change over time due to natural selection, with advantageous traits (e.g. camouflage) becoming more common in the population.

4419.belief: There are many misconceptions about evolution, including that because evolution by natural selection is a theory it is an untrustworthy explanation.
4419.statement: There are many misconceptions about evolution, including that because evolution by natural selection is a theory it is an untrustworthy explanation.
4419.correction: This lesson builds understanding that a scientific theory is a well evidenced and well tested explanation that is widely accepted by scientists, and also addresses some common misconceptions about evolution.

4962.belief: Non-infectious diseases such as heart disease can be passed from person to person.
4962.statement: Non-infectious diseases such as heart disease can be passed from person to person.
4962.correction: Only infectious diseases caused by pathogens can spread from person to person.

613.statement: Believing that we need oxygen to breathe.
613.correction: We breathe to get oxygen into our bodies so cells can use it as fuel for respiration.

2939.belief: All fat in the diet should be excluded.
2939.statement: All fat in the diet should be excluded.
2939.correction: Fat is vital for a healthy balanced diet. Unsaturated fats from plants help to build cell membranes.

479.belief: Asthma is a childhood disease that people will grow out of.
479.statement: Asthma is a childhood disease that people will grow out of.
479.correction: Although symptoms can improve as children get into adolescence, they will always have asthma and it may worsen as they get into old age.

3468.belief: The heart is heart shaped. The heart gets oxygen and glucose from the blood being pumped out.
3468.statement: The heart is heart shaped. The heart gets oxygen and glucose from the blood being pumped out.
3468.correction: Point out the shape of the heart and then reinforce with task B.

10781.belief: Vaping is harmless and the same as inhaling steam.
10781.statement: Vaping is harmless and the same as inhaling steam.
10781.correction: Vapes contain thousands of chemicals that have unknown effects.

578.belief: Because alcohol is legal it isn't as harmful as other drugs.
578.statement: Because alcohol is legal it isn't as harmful as other drugs.
578.correction: Alcohol is related to many lifestyle diseases. The WHO estimated 5 % of all deaths are related to alcohol.

4095.belief: Legal drugs cannot lead to addiction.
4095.statement: Legal drugs cannot lead to addiction.
4095.correction: Nearly all drugs used for recreation, legal or illegal, can lead to addiction.

9418.belief: Solvents only have very short-term effects.
9418.statement: Solvents only have very short-term effects.
9418.correction: Long-term solvent abuse can lead to brain damage and even death.

5565.belief: Plants do not reproduce sexually. Flowers are only produced to look attractive.
5565.statement: Plants do not reproduce sexually. Flowers are only produced to look attractive.
5565.correction: Show examples of the reproductive organs; discuss pollen and ova and relate them to gametes in humans.

5687.belief: Pollen are seeds, or that seeds are not made by sexual reproduction.
5687.statement: Pollen are seeds, or that seeds are not made by sexual reproduction.
5687.correction: Clearly show the difference between pollen as a gamete and the seeds as the offspring that grows into a new plant.

2699.belief: There is not enough food in the world, and that bees are the only pollinators.
2699.statement: There is not enough food in the world, and that bees are the only pollinators.
2699.correction: Emphasise that food distribution and nutrition is an issue in food security; also that there are many types of pollinator.

9169.correction: A seed is living, it contains an embryo and a food store and is a stage of development in the growth of offspring.

3735.belief: The independent variable is also measured, so this often gets confused with the dependent variable.
3735.statement: The independent variable is also measured, so this often gets confused with the dependent variable.
3735.correction: Use the definition for the dependent variable that it is being measured for the purpose of seeing what has happened at the end; the effect that the independent variable has had.

2417.belief: Displaying results in a table landscape with variables the wrong way round.
2417.statement: Displaying results in a table landscape with variables the wrong way round.
2417.correction: Clear descriptions and examples of correct tables.

4519.belief: Means are always divide by three.
4519.statement: That means are always divide by three.
4519.correction: Show examples where the number of repeats varies.

3986.belief: Labelling the x-axis with the values investigated instead of an evenly spaced range; or putting the axes the wrong way round for independent and dependent variables.
3986.statement: Labelling the x-axis with the values investigated instead of an evenly spaced range; or putting the axes the wrong way round for independent and dependent variables.
3986.correction: Clearly showing the placement of variables in the table and on the graphs, step-by-step guidance of drawing the graphs.

10267.statement: Thinking that agriculture just means growing crops.
10267.correction: The lesson explores the idea that agriculture also includes using land to rear animals, and that this has destroyed more habitat than using land to grow crops.

10273.belief: We can chop down and destroy forests without affecting ecosystems.
10273.statement: Thinking that we can chop down and destroy forests without affecting ecosystems.
10273.correction: The lessons explores how deforestation disrupts key processes in the carbon cycle and the water cycle, and how this can increase climate change, flooding, and put our food security at risk.

10302.belief: Species can choose or plan to evolve new adaptations to help them to survive climate change.
10302.statement: Thinking that species can choose or plan to evolve new adaptations to help them to survive climate change.
10302.correction: Part 2 of the lesson explores the idea that evolution occurs at random and may be too slow to save many species from climate change.

10296.belief: Plastic food packaging only has disadvantages, due to its effects as a pollutant in oceans and land ecosystems.
10296.statement: Thinking that plastic food packaging only has disadvantages, due to its effects as a pollutant in oceans and land ecosystems.
10296.correction: This lesson explores the advantages of plastic packaging in reducing food waste, alongside the risks it can pose to biodiversity.

7620.belief: All animals and plant are multicellular and that all unicellular organisms are bacteria.
7620.statement: Pupils may think that all animals and plant are multicellular and that all unicellular organisms are bacteria.
7620.correction: Lesson explicitly addresses this misconception and the questions in Task A are designed to expose the misconception.

289.belief: All animal cells are the same as the model animal cell. Energy is created during respiration.
289.statement: All animal cells are the same as the model animal cell. Energy is created during respiration.
289.correction: The model animal cell simplifies the complex structure of animal cells. There are specialised animal cells that have different shapes and sub-cellular structures to help them carry out a specific function. Energy is transferred through respiration.

5307.belief: A palisade cell is not a specialised cell as it is used as the plant cell model. All plant cells contain chloroplasts.
5307.statement: A palisade cell is not a specialised cell as it is used as the plant cell model. All plant cells contain chloroplasts.
5307.correction: Presentation outlines that the palisade cell is a specialised cell. Question in the check for understanding that is designed to show chloroplasts are not in root hair cells.

2762.correction: Addressed within the slides to specifically mention that some eukaryotic organisms are unicellular.

528.belief: All bacterial cells looks like the bacterial cell model.
528.statement: All bacterial cells looks like the bacterial cell model.
528.correction: Bacteria can come in different shapes and sizes, this will be outlined within the slide deck.

6201.statement: Pupils commonly convert units incorrectly, multiplying when they should divide or dividing when they should multiply.
6201.correction: It can help to relate the unit conversions in the lesson to an everyday example, e.g. pounds to pence.

2435.belief: All DNA codes for features rather than processes that are shared by all living organisms; also that animals are the only living organism that have DNA.
2435.statement: That all DNA codes for features rather than processes that are shared by all living organisms; also that animals are the only living organism that have DNA.
2435.correction: Make the role of DNA in features and processes explicit, using non-animal examples. Re-iterate the common processes of living organisms, and therefore why there are similarities in the genome.

2440.belief: DNA is living and not necessarily a chemical.
2440.statement: DNA is living and not necessarily a chemical.
2440.correction: Discussing that DNA is a chemical molecule and showing how it is made up of smaller chemical groups, and then modelling this chemical structure.

2946.belief: All features encoded in the genome are visible in the phenotype.
2946.statement: That all features encoded in the genome are visible in the phenotype.
2946.correction: Give examples of structural and functional proteins that are not visible in an organism's phenotype.

5473.belief: A person is either healthy or unhealthy.
5473.statement: A person is either healthy or unhealthy.
5473.correction: Health is a range from good to ill health.

3469.belief: The heart does not have its own blood vessels. Students often believe the heart gets oxygen and glucose from the blood circulating through it.
3469.statement: The heart does not have its own blood vessels. Students often believe the heart gets oxygen and glucose from the blood circulating through it.
3469.correction: The heart has its own blood supply through the coronary arteries.

7884.belief: Any health claim by a product must be true.
7884.statement: Pupils may think that any health claim by a product must be true.
7884.correction: Often no scientific research has been carried out on products claiming to be healthy.

4991.belief: There is nothing a person can do to decreases their risk of getting cancer.
4991.statement: There is nothing a person can do to decreases their risk of getting cancer.
4991.correction: Although we can't change inherited genetic risk factors for cancer, it does also have many associated lifestyle risk factors such as obesity and smoking.

8360.statement: Pupils may think that viruses are alive.
8360.correction: Viruses do not carry out many of the life processes required for living organisms such as respiration and reproduction.

4393.correction: Mosquitos are the vector that transfer the protist to humans.

3515.belief: HIV and AIDS are the same thing.
3515.statement: HIV and AIDS are the same thing.
3515.correction: HIV is the virus and AIDS is a consequence of late-stage HIV infection.

3553.belief: Only human and other animals can catch diseases. Plant diseases are not important.
3553.statement: Only human and other animals can catch diseases. Plant diseases are not important.
3553.correction: This lesson explores examples of plant diseases, the pathogens that cause them and how they are spread, and their devastating impacts.

10274.belief: Climate change affects the weather, but not human health.
10274.statement: Thinking that climate change affects the weather, but not human health.
10274.correction: This lesson explores direct and indirect impacts of climate change on human health.

1939.belief: Confusion often arises over which monomers are used to build which polymers.
1939.statement: Confusion often arises over which monomers are used to build which polymers.
1939.correction: The lesson clearly explores carbohydrates, proteins and lipids as separate sections and covers the monomers and the polymers they form with care and repetition.

4662.belief: Mistakes on method, results confusion, and poor descriptions using inaccurate terminology.
4662.statement: Mistakes on method, results confusion, and poor descriptions using inaccurate terminology.
4662.correction: Methods and results are described, demonstrated and tested throughout, and methods tried by pupils with results gathered and analysed. Repeated review of results occurs throughout the lesson, and methods and results are applied to novel questions.

5557.belief: Plants absorb nitrogen from the atmosphere, and animals do not need plants to obtain carbon, so plants are not necessary for food.
5557.statement: That plants absorb nitrogen from the atmosphere, and animals do not need plants to obtain carbon, so plants are not necessary for food.
5557.correction: How plants obtain carbon and nitrogen, and the reliance that consumers have on producers for these inorganic elements is covered in detail.

2712.belief: Enzymes are used up in reactions, or that an enzyme can catalyse many different reactions.
2712.statement: That enzymes are used up in reactions, or that an enzyme can catalyse many different reactions.
2712.correction: Enzymes are not used up in the reactions that they catalyse, and that they can only catalyse one reaction, as explained by the lock and key hypothesis.

2711.correction: The word denature is clearly introduced and a CfU explores the word die vs denature.

4639.belief: Misconceptions mixing aim and prediction or leaving them vague, writing a method which is unclear, and analysing hazards and their risks.
4639.statement: Misconceptions mixing aim and prediction or leaving them vague, writing a method which is unclear, and analysing hazards and their risks.
4639.correction: Approaches for stating aims and predictions, writing a method and dealing with variables, and analysing hazards and their risk are all covered with examples and practice tasks.

4660.belief: Mistakes are often made when preparing the practical, for instance which samples go into which test tubes, or carrying out the practical, such as exactly when to take the continuous sample.
4660.statement: Mistakes are often made when preparing the practical, for instance which samples go into which test tubes, or carrying out the practical, such as exactly when to take the continuous sample.
4660.correction: The correct approach to preparing and completing this method accurately and carefully is discussed throughout, with quick checks at key points and the opportunity to try it for themselves.

5488.belief: As pH increases above the optimum, enzymes denature and reaction rate falls, but this is not what happens at pHs below the optimum, so the graph and explanation resemble temperature.
5488.statement: As pH increases above the optimum, enzymes denature and reaction rate falls, but this is not what happens at pHs below the optimum, so the graph and explanation resemble temperature.
5488.correction: The process of denaturing an enzyme is explored in detail, and a graph of reaction rate is explained carefully to make it clear that the changes to rate occur above and below the optimum pH.

5031.belief: Nutrients and waste are either not produced, or not by every cell, with misconceptions about where these substances come from or go to and what the roles of the various systems are as a result.
5031.statement: Nutrients and waste are either not produced, or not by every cell, with misconceptions about where these substances come from or go to and what the roles of the various systems are as a result.
5031.correction: Key nutrients and waste products are dealt with individually and related to the relevant body systems. These ideas are focused on in main and check tasks.

1952.belief: Confusion between the names and functions of the different parts of the heart and the direction that blood moves through the heart.
1952.statement: Confusion between the names and functions of the different parts of the heart and the direction that blood moves through the heart.
1952.correction: The parts of the heart and their structure and function are dealt with separately and clearly, and followed up with quick checks plus longer and more detailed tasks.

4807.belief: The names of the blood vessels and their functions and adaptations are often confused. Students often forget or misunderstand red blood cell adaptations too.
4807.statement: The names of the blood vessels and their functions and adaptations are often confused. Students often forget or misunderstand red blood cell adaptations too.
4807.correction: Both these areas are covered in detail, with clear step-by-step information given and tasks to check learning and reinforce understanding.

9127.belief: Scientific drawings made using a microscope are difficult to do and often sketched like an artwork. The requirements are clear and precise and require practise to get right.
9127.statement: Scientific drawings made using a microscope are difficult to do and often sketched like an artwork. The requirements are clear and precise and require practise to get right.
9127.correction: The expectations for scientific drawings are clearly stated and shown visually. Opportunities to practise drawing different structures are included throughout the lesson.

4657.belief: Mistakes with the definitions of diffusion, osmosis and active transport are common, as are their application to biological scenarios.
4657.statement: Mistakes with the definitions of diffusion, osmosis and active transport are common, as are their application to biological scenarios.
4657.correction: The definitions are clearly stated and contextualised using key human biological processes and examples.

4654.belief: Mistakes with the calculations of surface area or volume are common. The concepts of surface area, volume and their ratio, with the effect that changing these have on diffusion, are difficult.
4654.statement: Mistakes with the calculations of surface area or volume are common. The concepts of surface area, volume and their ratio, with the effect that changing these have on diffusion, are difficult.
4654.correction: Plenty of practise on how to calculate surface area and volume, and compare these as a ratio, some simplified, is included. The experiment results are used to show the impact of changing surface area, volume and width on diffusion.

8359.belief: Villi and alveoli increase surface area without changing volume.
8359.statement: Pupils may think that villi and alveoli increase surface area without changing volume.
8359.correction: These ideas are explored in detail with examples and demonstrations using cube animals. The issue of surface area to volume ratio and diffusion rate is covered thoroughly, along with solutions to the issues in humans.

4754.belief: There are multiple misunderstandings about the nervous system, including the order and function of neurones, the roles of the stimulus, receptor and effector, and the central and peripheral parts.
4754.statement: There are multiple misunderstandings about the nervous system, including the order and function of neurones, the roles of the stimulus, receptor and effector, and the central and peripheral parts.
4754.correction: The pathway through the nervous system is built up with examples and demonstrated as a flowchart. The roles of the different parts is explained and practised, and distinctions are made between the central and peripheral parts.

10767.belief: There is usually a lot of confusion over the synapse and how the signal moves from electrical, to chemical, to electrical again. There are many new key words involved, which makes it even harder.
10767.statement: There is usually a lot of confusion over the synapse and how the signal moves from electrical, to chemical, to electrical again. There are many new key words involved, which makes it even harder.
10767.correction: The synapse has been broken down into several stages with clear diagrams and carefully used key words. There are plenty of opportunities to practise using the terminology and explaining the process, including applying it to a real-world scenario.

2258.belief: Describing and identifying independent, dependent and control variables and following a method with care and accuracy are skills that take time to build and need frequent revisiting.
2258.statement: Describing and identifying independent, dependent and control variables and following a method with care and accuracy are skills that take time to build and need frequent revisiting.
2258.correction: The variables in the practical and the method are outlined and discussed. Considerations on the ethicality of the experiment due to human subjects, and the presence of anomalous data, are also covered in detail.

1998.belief: What constitutes a reflex response, and how they are generated in the body is often confused and muddled, leading to an incorrect mix between a standard neural pathway and the reflex pathway.
1998.statement: What constitutes a reflex response, and how they are generated in the body is often confused and muddled, leading to an incorrect mix between a standard neural pathway and the reflex pathway.
1998.correction: The reflex pathway is clearly stated and explained, and it is compared to the standard neural pathway. Plenty of examples of reflexes are given, including those that occur in other organisms, and there is a quick practical to try too.

1955.belief: There is often confusion between parts of the eye and their function, and that both the cornea and the lens refract light, but only the lens can focus light.
1955.statement: There is often confusion between parts of the eye and their function, and that both the cornea and the lens refract light, but only the lens can focus light.
1955.correction: The parts of the eye and their function are covered carefully and in detail. The role of the cornea and lens in refracting and focusing light is examined in detail with simplified drawings to demonstrate.

4656.belief: Mistakes with the defects and treatments in vision caused by long- and short-sightedness (e.g. getting the symptoms or the type of lenses mixed up) or how lenses actually correct vision are common.
4656.statement: Mistakes with the defects and treatments in vision caused by long- and short-sightedness (e.g. getting the symptoms or the type of lenses mixed up) or how lenses actually correct vision are common.
4656.correction: The conditions are dealt with separately with clear and concise information conveyed and supported with diagrams and reinforced with questions that focus on these mistakes and misconceptions.

1941.belief: Confusion around which functions of the brain operate where, the level of detail required, and how these functions can become impaired through injury or disease are common.
1941.statement: Confusion around which functions of the brain operate where, the level of detail required, and how these functions can become impaired through injury or disease are common.
1941.correction: The role and parts of the brain are covered in detail and separately to avoid confusion. Quick checks and tasks focus on areas of misunderstanding to reinforce the correct message and help identify those who have got it wrong.

7899.belief: All hormones in the body form part of the reproductive system and its regulation.
7899.statement: Pupils may think that all hormones in the body form part of the reproductive system and its regulation.
7899.correction: The slide deck gives specific examples of hormones that are not part of the reproductive system; this includes the example of antagonistic hormones.

4220.belief: Not linking the idea that glucose concentration is important for cellular respiration, even during times of rest.
4220.statement: Not linking the idea that glucose concentration is important for cellular respiration, even during times of rest.
4220.correction: There are a selection of slides in LC2 that specifically link glucose and respiration and discuss the idea of respiration occurring during rest.

10495.belief: Type 1 diabetes is caused by lifestyle, particularly poor diet.
10495.statement: Type 1 diabetes is caused by lifestyle, particularly poor diet.
10495.correction: The slide deck states that type 1 diabetes is caused by genes or environmental factors and there is a question in task A to assess this. In contrast there is a big focus on lifestyle and obesity being linked to developing type 2 diabetes.

1792.belief: It is a common misconception that consumers (including humans) could survive without producers.
1792.statement: It is a common misconception that consumers (including humans) could survive without producers.
1792.correction: The dependence of consumers on photosynthesis in producers in explored in depth.

4678.belief: Mixing up a prediction, an observation and an explanation.
4678.statement: Mixing up a prediction, an observation and an explanation.
4678.correction: This practical lesson explores predictions, observations and explanations in the context of using iodine solution to test leaves for starch.

2451.belief: A dominant condition is 'stronger' and that only the strongest characteristic is inherited from one parent.
2451.statement: A dominant condition is 'stronger' and that only the strongest characteristic is inherited from one parent.
2451.correction: Two genes are inherited, so both alleles contribute to the genotype. In some cases one is dominant and therefore will always be expressed (through protein structure) in the phenotype, the recessive allele is still present.

3209.belief: A gamete has two alleles, Punnett square has too many alleles for gametes. Also that only four offspring are produced and therefore each will definitely have the genotype and phenotype shown.
3209.statement: A gamete has two alleles, Punnett square has too many alleles for gametes. Also that only four offspring are produced and therefore each will definitely have the genotype and phenotype shown.
3209.correction: Model the alleles within gametes so it is clear. Refer to half the gametes having each version, moving away from the idea of divisions of 4.

2450.belief: The dominant allele is stronger than the recessive allele preventing its expression or that the recessive allele is an absence of the dominant allele, also that all genetic disorders are recessive.
2450.statement: The dominant allele is stronger than the recessive allele preventing its expression or that the recessive allele is an absence of the dominant allele, also that all genetic disorders are recessive.
2450.correction: Linking the allele to change in protein structure, showing that proteins are produced in the case of dominant and recessive alleles. Examples of dominant and recessive disorders provided.

10467.belief: Two genes are inherited, both alleles contribute to the genotype; scientists work in isolation from one another.
10467.statement: Two genes are inherited, both alleles contribute to the genotype; scientists work in isolation from one another.
10467.correction: Keep repeating that alleles are different codes for the same protein, different proteins lead to different traits (phenotypes). Scientists build on the work of others, and critique each other's work, to build a better understanding.

4400.correction: Males have one Y and one X chromosome.

4753.belief: Multicellular organisms reproduce by cell division like unicellular organisms.
4753.statement: Multicellular organisms reproduce by cell division like unicellular organisms.
4753.correction: Multicellular organisms use cell division for reproduction. A non-example will be used to show reproduction is not part of reproduction in multicellular organisms.

1662.belief: Chromosomes are halved when the cell splits.
1662.statement: Chromosomes are halved when the cell splits.
1662.correction: Slides repeatedly address the concept that chromosomes are copied.

9950.belief: Each strand of DNA is the same without recognising one strand is inverted.
9950.statement: Students may think that each strand of DNA is the same without recognising one strand is inverted.
9950.correction: The slides specifically mention the second strand is inverted and this is also reinforced using diagrams of inverted nucleotides wherever possible.

8333.belief: All tumours are cancerous and dangerous.
8333.statement: Pupils may think that all tumours are cancerous and dangerous.
8333.correction: Pupils are given very clear examples of the difference between benign and malignant tumours. The difference between the two is covered in the slide deck, check for understanding questions and practice tasks.

3974.belief: Knowing the differences between mitosis and meiosis. In particular when they are used, the number of cell divisions and if variation is present.
3974.statement: Knowing the differences between mitosis and meiosis. In particular when they are used, the number of cell divisions and if variation is present.
3974.correction: The final learning cycle of the lesson serves to compare the features of mitosis and meiosis, this includes CFU questions and a practice task.

305.belief: Only animals are multicellular; that specialised cells are individual; all DNA in a cell is the same so will produce the same proteins.
305.statement: Only animals are multicellular; that specialised cells are individual; all DNA in a cell is the same so will produce the same proteins.
305.correction: Examples of multicellular plants, with specialised cells, tissues and organs provided; show images of cells as tissues rather than just individual. All cells have the same DNA, but it is whether the genes are turned on that makes them specialise.

165.belief: Adult stem cells don't exist or can differentiate in the same way as embryonic stem cells.
165.statement: Adult stem cells don't exist or can differentiate in the same way as embryonic stem cells.
165.correction: Give examples of adult stem cells and the types of cells they will differentiate into, using examples that pupils might be familiar with.

9017.belief: Roots are not a tissue of the plant, or contain living cells, also that wood is not made of living cells.
9017.statement: Roots are not a tissue of the plant, or contain living cells, also that wood is not made of living cells.
9017.correction: Show the cells of roots and how they divide to allow the length and width of the root to grow; also the rings on trees that indicate new cell division in the trunk of a tree.

9604.belief: Stem cells can treat more diseases than they have been proved to. All stem cells used are taken from embryos.
9604.statement: That stem cells can treat more diseases than they have been proved to. All stem cells used are taken from embryos.
9604.correction: Introducing the idea of induced stem cells and adult stem cells in treatments, but also that the main use is in research rather than full treatment of a disease or condition.

9810.statement: Students often struggle to remember that any organism (not just animals) can become a fossil
9810.correction: This is addressed in the lesson by including examples of fossilised plant and cell material. The first practice task also addresses this misconception.

9812.statement: Students often struggle to understand the concept of having a common ancestor and confuse it with one species being descended from another.
9812.correction: This lesson uses evolutionary trees to help students visualise the relationships between groups of organisms.

9751.statement: Students often forget that selective breeding is a process that happens over many generations.
9751.correction: This lesson includes examples of how to describe the process of selective breeding.

4443.belief: Many students believe that Darwin was the only scientist involved in the development of the theory of evolution by natural selection.
4443.statement: Many students believe that Darwin was the only scientist involved in the development of the theory of evolution by natural selection.
4443.correction: This lesson directly addresses this misconception and includes examples of other scientists who were involved in the original and later development of the theory.

9823.belief: Animals choose to adapt themselves to their environment.
9823.statement: Students often think that animals choose to adapt themselves to their environment.
9823.correction: The language in this lesson has been specifically chosen to avoid embedding this misconception and CfUs help expose this misconception in student thinking.

9544.belief: All species will be able to evolve to cope with climate change.
9544.statement: All species will be able to evolve to cope with climate change.
9544.correction: The lesson explores why not all species will be able to evolve fast enough to adapt to the pace of climate change.

10788.belief: Varying the population size of an organism will not affect an ecosystem.
10788.statement: Varying the population size of an organism will not affect an ecosystem.
10788.correction: All organisms are important within an ecosystem. If one organism's population size changes, either as a result of a biotic factor (predation / disease) or an abiotic factor, it will affect all organisms within the ecosystem (to varying degrees).

4426.belief: Many pupils believe that in order to determine a population size within a habitat, all organisms within a habitat have to be counted.
4426.statement: Many pupils believe that in order to determine a population size within a habitat, all organisms within a habitat have to be counted.
4426.correction: Populations can be estimated using sampling techniques. As long as a sample size is large enough, it will provide a reliable estimate of the population size. Pupils should understand that counting all individuals in a habitat is very difficult to do.

8692.belief: Quadrats can be used to give an accurate picture of a habitat or ecosystem.
8692.statement: Quadrats can be used to give an accurate picture of a habitat or ecosystem.
8692.correction: Sampling using a quadrat provides only a snapshot of a specific area at a specific time. To give a more accurate understanding, quadrat samples should be taken over a long period to provide a fuller picture of a habitat or ecosystem.

8691.belief: Quadrats must always be randomly placed to survey organisms.
8691.statement: Quadrats must always be randomly placed to survey organisms.
8691.correction: Quadrats can be systematically placed as part of sampling activities. This is not random sampling but regular sampling.

5246.belief: Organisms are able to quickly adapt to the place where they live.
5246.statement: That organisms are able to quickly adapt to the place where they live.
5246.correction: Referring to inheritance, explain that changes to organisms take time to evolve - responses to any environmental change is not instant. In some organisms, where reproduction is slow, responses can be too slow to avoid extinction.

2208.belief: Decomposers release energy that is recycled back to plants.
2208.statement: Decomposers release energy that is recycled back to plants.
2208.correction: Decomposers break down dead organisms and waste. This returns minerals to the soil which can be used by plants. It is worth stating that some decomposers are eaten by carnivores as part of food chain diagrams that include decomposers.

8907.belief: Research has found that pupils generally do not appreciate the important roles of microorganisms in decomposition and the recycling of elements. Many associate microorganisms only with disease.
8907.statement: Research has found that pupils generally do not appreciate the important roles of microorganisms in decomposition and the recycling of elements. Many associate microorganisms only with disease.
8907.correction: The lesson outlines the factors that are important in recycling of elements but also that microorganisms are the natural cleaners of the environment.

9225.belief: Several liquids are measured in this practical. The equipment used to measure the lipase should not be used to measure the liquids or the lipase may begin to digest fats before the practical starts.
9225.statement: Several liquids are measured in this practical. The equipment used to measure the lipase should not be used to measure the liquids or the lipase may begin to digest fats before the practical starts.
9225.correction: To prevent contamination, ensure that the method is explained carefully and modelled through a demonstration or by watching the practical video.

484.belief: The atmosphere is made up of mainly oxygen and carbon dioxide.
484.statement: The atmosphere is made up of mainly oxygen and carbon dioxide.
484.correction: Explain that Earth's atmosphere is delicately balanced. There is enough oxygen to maintain life, and enough carbon dioxide to help insulate the planet, maintaining the temperature that allows life to exist.

10929.belief: The water cycle only includes the processes of evaporation from the Earth's surface to the atmosphere and condensation returning water to the Earth.
10929.statement: The water cycle only includes the processes of evaporation from the Earth's surface to the atmosphere and condensation returning water to the Earth.
10929.correction: There is exemplification of how the water cycle involves percolation of water into the ground and how plants use this water. Some of this is released by transpiration.

6167.statement: Pupils may believe that viruses are alive.
6167.correction: Viruses are not cells. They do not carry out many of the processes of living organisms such as replication and respiration.

7753.belief: Daughter cells have different DNA to the parent cell.
7753.statement: Pupils may think that daughter cells have different DNA to the parent cell.
7753.correction: Slides repeatedly address the concept that DNA is copied and that daughter cells are genetically identical.

8797.belief: Recognising the difference between images of interphase and prophase. In particular, the idea of DNA condensing to form visible chromosomes during prophase.
8797.statement: Recognising the difference between images of interphase and prophase. In particular, the idea of DNA condensing to form visible chromosomes during prophase.
8797.correction: There are two slides that aim to show the difference between DNA held within the nucleus and visible chromosomes where DNA has condensed. There is also a check for understanding question and practise task question to reinforce this concept.

8107.belief: People are either healthy or unhealthy.
8107.statement: Pupils may think that people are either healthy or unhealthy.
8107.correction: Health is a range from good to ill. Fitness is one indicator of general health.

10878.correction: Viruses do not carry out many of the life processes required for living organisms such as respiration and reproduction.

8796.belief: Recognising that after cell growth DNA condenses to form visible chromosomes and the nuclear membrane breaks down.
8796.statement: Recognising that after cell growth DNA condenses to form visible chromosomes and the nuclear membrane breaks down.
8796.correction: There are slides that aim to show the difference between DNA held within the nucleus and visible chromosomes where DNA has condensed. There is also a check for understanding question and practice task question to reinforce this concept.

3227.belief: Genes, DNA and chromosomes are used interchangeably rather than understanding their separate definitions; also that organisms such as animals and plants are not related.
3227.statement: Genes, DNA and chromosomes are used interchangeably rather than understanding their separate definitions; also that organisms such as animals and plants are not related.
3227.correction: Use images to show the difference between DNA, genes and chromosomes; display a phylogenetic tree so the common ancestry of all living organisms can be visualised and so the commonality of DNA between all life.

2437.belief: DNA is the endpoint of a characteristic rather than the fact that it codes for proteins that give a protein; also that all characteristics are visible.
2437.statement: DNA is the endpoint of a characteristic rather than the fact that it codes for proteins that give a protein; also that all characteristics are visible.
2437.correction: Clear examples, analogies and models to show the code in genes, leads to the order of an amino acids in a protein; examples of structural and functional proteins.

4672.belief: Mixing up amino acids and nucleotides, also nucleotides and bases.
4672.statement: Mixing up amino acids and nucleotides, also nucleotides and bases.
4672.correction: Activity checks: Nucleotides contain a base; DNA is a polymer of nucleotides that codes for the order of amino acids in a protein.

4795.belief: Mutations always have a negative effect on an organism.
4795.statement: Mutations always have a negative effect on an organism.
4795.correction: Mutations can produce variation in a phenotype by producing alleles of a gene.

2438.belief: All DNA is genes that code for proteins; and that our characteristics are only affected by our genes.
2438.statement: All DNA is genes that code for proteins; and that our characteristics are only affected by our genes
2438.correction: Most of the DNA is non-coding (non-genes), and controls when genes are expressed (i.e. when proteins are made). Changes (genetic variants) in non-coding DNA can affect characteristics (phenotype) as they control whether a gene is expressed or not.

10536.belief: Understanding the ethics of research practices is complex and often misunderstood. The details of various brain scanning techniques are complex and also confusing.
10536.statement: Understanding the ethics of research practices is complex and often misunderstood. The details of various brain scanning techniques are complex and also confusing.
10536.correction: Ethical practices are discussed with examples and changes through history to give context. Brain scanning techniques are illustrated and explained, with follow up tasks.

4912.belief: Negative feedback only works to reverse high levels back to normal.
4912.statement: Negative feedback only works to reverse high levels back to normal.
4912.correction: The slide deck has several slides where changes are described as being high and low and there is a CFU question in the final learning cycle that specifically assesses this misconception.

1801.belief: It is a common misconception to think that light (or energy) is a substance and a chemical reactant in photosynthesis that is converted into glucose.
1801.statement: It is a common misconception to think that light (or energy) is a substance and a chemical reactant in photosynthesis that is converted into glucose.
1801.correction: The role of light in transferring energy to chlorophyll for photosynthesis is explored.

1797.belief: A common misconception is that photosynthesis is just one simple reaction, as depicted by the word equation and balanced symbol equation.
1797.statement: A common misconception is that photosynthesis is just one simple reaction, as depicted by the word equation and balanced symbol equation.
1797.correction: This explores the idea that the word equation and balanced symbol equation are useful but very simple models of photosynthesis, and also explores a slightly more detailed two-stage model of the process.

10461.belief: All tumours are cancerous and dangerous.
10461.statement: All tumours are cancerous and dangerous.
10461.correction: Students are given very clear examples of the difference between benign and malignant tumours. The difference between the two is covered in the slide deck, check for understanding questions and practice tasks.

4401.belief: Males only have Y chromosomes, only males inherit sex-linked conditions.
4401.statement: Males only have Y chromosomes, only males inherit sex-linked conditions.
4401.correction: Males have one Y and one X chromosome, males only need one recessive allele to suffer from a sex-linked genetic disorder, whereas females need two and therefore the condition is less common in females.

692.belief: All blood cells protect us against pathogens.
692.statement: All blood cells protect us against pathogens.
692.correction: White blood cells are part of the immune system that protects us against pathogens. Red blood cells transport oxygen to cells. Platelets are not cells, but they do help to protect against pathogens by helping to seal wounds.

4679.belief: Mixing up scientific terms such as antigen and antibody.
4679.statement: Mixing up scientific terms such as antigen and antibody.
4679.correction: The lesson explores the relationship and differences between antigens, antibodies and antitoxins.

336.belief: Antibodies remain in the blood for years, which makes a person immune to a disease.
336.statement: Antibodies remain in the blood for years, which makes a person immune to a disease.
336.correction: Antibodies don't stay in the body longer term, the memory cells do and they provide long lasting immunity against a pathogen.

4683.correction: The study by Dr Wakefield is highly flawed, and has been discredited. Many subsequent studies have found no link between the MMR vaccination and autism. Measles is a highly infectious disease that can have devastating consequences.

5559.belief: Plants have no defence against pests or pathogens.
5559.statement: Plants have no defence against pests or pathogens.
5559.correction: Plants have physical, chemical and mechanical defences against pathogens.

9755.statement: Students frequently write in exams that respiration "creates" energy.
9755.correction: This lesson contains checks and practice tasks that address this misconception.

9917.belief: Plants don't respire, and that they (only) photosynthesise instead.
9917.statement: Students sometimes think that plants don't respire, and that they (only) photosynthesise instead.
9917.correction: This lesson contains examples of plants respiring.

7107.statement: Pupils often read the volume of gas incorrectly as they do not measure it from the bottom of the meniscus of the water in the measuring cylinder.
7107.correction: This lesson contains a detailed explanation of how to correctly measure volumes from the meniscus, and why this is important.

10278.belief: Each enzyme can act on many different substrates.
10278.statement: Thinking that each enzyme can act on many different substrates.
10278.correction: This lesson reinforces understanding that each enzyme has a specific substrate, because only that substrate will fit into they enzyme's active site.

4637.belief: A misconception that is often seen is that there is a build up of biomass along a food chain.
4637.statement: A misconception that is often seen is that there is a build up of biomass along a food chain.
4637.correction: The lesson outlines how biomass is actually lost between trophic levels through life processes.

1799.belief: A common misconception is that a small increase in greenhouse gases and a small rise in Earth's temperature will not have much impact on organisms on Earth beyond polar ice melting.
1799.statement: A common misconception is that a small increase in greenhouse gases and a small rise in Earth's temperature will not have much impact on organisms on Earth beyond polar ice melting.
1799.correction: The lesson outlines how human activities increase the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere and how this links to climate change. The lesson also outlines how climate change impacts life on Earth.

1793.belief: A common misconception is that the excessive growth of the plants in eutrophication is the cause of a reduction in biodiversity as a result of the plants using up the oxygen in the water.
1793.statement: A common misconception is that the excessive growth of the plants in eutrophication is the cause of a reduction in biodiversity as a result of the plants using up the oxygen in the water.
1793.correction: Steps in eutrophication are outlined. Increased minerals cause the growth of plants at the surface resulting in the death and decomposition of the plants. Decomposing dead organic matter results in micro-organisms using oxygen and biodiversity loss.

1984.belief: The conservation of biodiversity can only happen on a large scale, e.g. through protecting large areas of habitat.
1984.statement: The conservation of biodiversity can only happen on a large scale, e.g. through protecting large areas of habitat.
1984.correction: Biodiversity conservation can take place on a small scale, for example, by providing habitats in gardens and in urban areas.

6033.statement: Pupils may have a belief that genetically engineered organisms are not safe. While there are risks with GM organisms, there are a wide range of benefits which can help humans.
6033.correction: The lesson highlights the benefits of genetically modifying crops to address food security challenges, especially in the context of a growing human population and other factors that threaten food availability.

3722.belief: Incorrectly thinking that we can use and damage forests and oceans without negative consequences for the planet and our own survival.
3722.statement: Incorrectly thinking that we can use and damage forests and oceans without negative consequences for the planet and our own survival.
3722.correction: This lesson explores the crucial role of forests and oceans as global carbon sinks that offset human carbon emissions, and the impacts of deforestation, global warming and ocean acidification.

9786.statement: Some students do not realise the significance of the shape of the root hair cell and do not explain this in terms of increasing its surface area.
9786.correction: The idea of surface area as the significant adaptation of root hair cells is clearly introduced, checked, and reinforced with specific tasks that explicitly enquire about this adaptation.

9736.belief: If students fail to understand that water only enters the plant at the roots, and not through the leaves, then the process of transpiration will be very muddled and confused.
9736.statement: If students fail to understand that water only enters the plant at the roots, and not through the leaves, then the process of transpiration will be very muddled and confused.
9736.correction: The lesson reinforces the pathway that water takes through the plant, clearly stating that water enters at the roots, and showing several times how it moves up through xylem.

10295.belief: Plants have stomata in equal numbers on every surface of their leaves.
10295.statement: Thinking that plants have stomata in equal numbers on every surface of their leaves.
10295.correction: Through practical work and data analysis, pupils explore the distribution of stomata on the top and bottom surfaces of leaves.

9757.statement: Students get confused between transport in the xylem (water and minerals) and the phloem (sugars).
9757.correction: These sections are covered in separate lessons, each with clear explanations and reinforcing tasks to support learning.

3708.belief: Incorrectly calculating the total magnification by adding the magnification of the eyepiece lens to the magnification of the objective lens.
3708.statement: Incorrectly calculating the total magnification by adding the magnification of the eyepiece lens to the magnification of the objective lens.
3708.correction: The correct way to calculate the total magnification (by multiplying the magnification of the eyepiece lens by the magnification of the objective lens) is practiced.

51.belief: Being able to explain the set up of a potometer is difficult because it has so many stages that are tricky.
51.statement: Being able to explain the set up of a potometer is difficult because it has so many stages that are tricky.
51.correction: The stages of setting up a potometer are broken down into four parts, checked for understanding, reinforced with a lab demonstration video and concluded with a cartoon task.

9807.statement: Some students may struggle to explain how transpiration is affected by a number of factors, even though these factors have the same effects on everyday activities such as drying hair or clothes.
9807.correction: Links between these everyday events and transpiration have been made and illustrated simultaneously, so students make the link between the two.

9808.statement: Students struggle with the idea that plants have organs and systems like humans, and that all these systems and cells are adapted with specialised features to enable them to do their job effectively.
9808.correction: The plant vascular system and human circulatory system have been compared, and human lung alveoli and digestive system villi have been compared with root hair cells.

3530.belief: Hormones are only released in the brain and control the mood.
3530.statement: Hormones are only released in the brain and control the mood.
3530.correction: Hormones control many processes in the body and are secreted from many glands. Those involved in puberty and the menstrual cycle have physical effects that may also impact on mood.

2025.belief: The contraceptive pill can protect from STIs; that all contraception is 100% effective; there are no side effects to hormonal contraception.
2025.statement: The contraceptive pill can protect from STIs; that all contraception is 100% effective; there are no side effects to hormonal contraception.
2025.correction: Discuss barrier methods and their benefit in preventing STIs, oral contraceptive can be affected by user error or illness. Oral contraception has side effects but these are less in modern times.

8142.belief: Plants move towards the sun, rather than grow in that direction. Pupils may also think that plants are not living.
8142.statement: Pupils may think that plants move towards the sun, rather than grow in that direction. Pupils may also think that plants are not living.
8142.correction: Plants grow in a certain direction through mitosis (in meristem) and elongation. Plants are living as they carry out the common processes of living organisms.

7643.belief: Auxins move down the side of the stem that is nearest to the light and cause it to bend. Pupils may also think that sketched drawings are more accurate than scientific line drawings.
7643.statement: Pupils may think auxins move down the side of the stem that is nearest to the light and cause it to bend. Pupils may also think that sketched drawings are more accurate than scientific line drawings.
7643.correction: Auxins move down the shaded side causing cell elongation, which causes the seedling to grow towards the light. Line diagrams are representations that are clear and labelled; making them easy to read.

7782.belief: A drawing must be as realistic as possible hence sketching is encouraged. Pupils may also think that roots will continue to grow in the direction that they start.
7782.statement: Pupils may think that a drawing must be as realistic as possible hence sketching is encouraged. Pupils may also think that roots will continue to grow in the direction that they start.
7782.correction: Emphasise that a line diagram is a simple representation of an object so sketching is not best practise. This lesson explains how roots will grow in the direction of gravity even if their orientation is changed.

2044.belief: Coordinating the measurements and the sugar solution in this practical is fiddly and if not done methodically, the results can be easily confused.
2044.statement: Coordinating the measurements and the sugar solution in this practical is fiddly and if not done methodically, the results can be easily confused.
2044.correction: The table in which results will be recorded is clearly labelled and used, and a copy is provided in the worksheet.

4653.belief: Mistakes around calculating change in percentage mass are common, as are misunderstandings around why changes in mass occur.
4653.statement: Mistakes around calculating change in percentage mass are common, as are misunderstandings around why changes in mass occur.
4653.correction: The calculations for percentage mass are introduced and walked through with an 'I-do, we-do, you-do' model. There are plenty of calculations to practice on. Why mass changes occur is also covered in detail and with supporting diagrams.

1813.belief: It is common for pupils to misunderstand the links between increased or decreased body temperature and the impact on enzyme function.
1813.statement: It is common for pupils to misunderstand the links between increased or decreased body temperature and the impact on enzyme function.
1813.correction: Explanations of the effect of temperature on enzyme activity, the link between body temperature and enzyme function, and conditions such as hyper- and hypo-thermia are made and explored in this lesson.

10543.belief: Understanding why the physiological responses to higher or lower body temperatures occur is often confused, because although the processes themselves are familiar, the reasons behind them are not.
10543.statement: Understanding why the physiological responses to higher or lower body temperatures occur is often confused, because although the processes themselves are familiar, the reasons behind them are not.
10543.correction: Detail has been included to explain carefully and one at a time the reasons for a range of physiological responses to high or low body temperature, and these are illustrated with clear, familiar diagrams.

4640.belief: Misconceptions about the roles of the kidneys, bladder and how the blood is 'cleaned' exist. Students often conflate/confuse these roles, muddle key terms or offer weak descriptions or explanations.
4640.statement: Misconceptions about the roles of the kidneys, bladder and how the blood is 'cleaned' exist. Students often conflate/confuse these roles, muddle key terms or offer weak descriptions or explanations.
4640.correction: The roles of the kidney and bladder are clearly described, and diagrams and flowcharts are used to support the detailed explanations. Tasks that reinforce understanding and check for clarity and correct use of key words are included too.

9775.statement: Students may mistakenly believe that only one factor can limit the rate of photosynthesis at any given time.
9775.correction: The lesson teaches that multiple factors, such as light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, and temperature, can simultaneously influence the rate of photosynthesis.

6307.statement: Some pupils do not consider how to control variables carefully enough. This means results are likely to be less accurate and so do not provide conclusions that can be used to support a hypothesis.
6307.correction: Each type of variable is considered during the lesson and repeated to help pupils to understand the differences between each type of variable.

7350.statement: Pupils often struggle with the difference between repeatability and reproducibility.
7350.correction: The lesson outlines the difference between these two aspects of working scientifically and checks pupils understanding of these in relation to the investigation.

7625.statement: Pupils may think that antibiotics work on all pathogens.
7625.correction: Antibiotics only kill bacteria. Antibiotics can only kill certain bacteria and so the doctor will prescribe the correct one.

7626.belief: All antimicrobial substances are equally effective against all microorganisms.
7626.statement: Pupils may think that all antimicrobial substances are equally effective against all microorganisms.
7626.correction: The effectiveness of different antimicrobial substances against bacteria can be tested.

8554.statement: Pupils often use the diameter instead of the radius when calculating the area of a clear zone of inhibition around a disc.
8554.correction: Remind pupils that we use 𝜋r² to calculate the area, so they need to find the radius first.

7111.statement: Pupils often do not realise that drugs are tested on healthy individuals first.
7111.correction: Healthy individuals are used as they will not have symptoms that interfere with the side effects from the drug.

9771.statement: Students have many misconceptions about DNA including, for example, that DNA is alive.
9771.correction: This lesson includes dual coded diagrams of DNA to help avoid embedding misconceptions.

4447.belief: Many students write that organisms change themselves to become better adapted to their environment.
4447.statement: Many students write that organisms change themselves to become better adapted to their environment.
4447.correction: This lesson contains checks for this misconception and challenges it with examples of natural selection explained at the genetic level.

7646.belief: Bacteria are not living organisms and/or do not evolve. Pupils may also think that all bacteria are harmful.
7646.statement: Pupils may think that bacteria are not living organisms and/or do not evolve. Pupils may also think that all bacteria are harmful.
7646.correction: The lesson explores two examples of evolution in bacteria, explaining each example through mutation, reproduction and natural selection.

4444.belief: Many students will hold the misconception that "complex" organisms (e.g. animals) use sexual reproduction and "simple" organisms (e.g. plants, microorganisms) use asexual reproduction to reproduce.
4444.statement: Many students will hold the misconception that "complex" organisms (e.g. animals) use sexual reproduction and "simple" organisms (e.g. plants, microorganisms) use asexual reproduction to reproduce.
4444.correction: This lesson includes examples of plants and animals carrying out asexual and sexual reproduction.

7819.belief: All eukaryotic cells have the same cell components.
7819.statement: Pupils might think that all eukaryotic cells have the same cell components.
7819.correction: Draw pupils' attention to the differences between the different types of eukaryotic cells. Focus on the presence of a nucleus, mitochondria, and, in plant cells, chloroplasts, as identifying characteristics of eukaryotic cells.

7684.belief: All cells are approximately the same size.
7684.statement: Pupils might think that all cells are approximately the same size.
7684.correction: Calculations in the deck will allow pupils to compare the relative sizes of cells. It might be helpful to draw extra attention to this point.

8011.belief: The modern classification system that we use today is complete.
8011.statement: Pupils may think that the modern classification system that we use today is complete.
8011.correction: Remind pupils why new data from experiments or observations leads to changes in models or theories.

5248.belief: Organisms evolve over a short period of time.
5248.statement: Organisms evolve over a short period of time.
5248.correction: Draw pupils attention to the tome scales on the evolutionary trees to show that evolution takes place slowly over long periods of time.

2755.belief: Over-estimating the risks of genetic engineering and genetically modified (GM) organisms.
2755.statement: Over-estimating the risks of genetic engineering and genetically modified (GM) organisms.
2755.correction: The lesson explores the need to weigh up possible benefits, risks and ethical questions when making decisions about genetic engineering.

10268.belief: An allele that increases the risk of a disease makes it certain to happen.
10268.statement: Thinking that an allele that increases the risk of a disease makes it certain to happen.
10268.correction: The lesson explores the idea the alleles can be risk factors for disease, and that in many cases other factors also affect the risk.

10266.belief: Abortion is the only option following a positive genetic test result during pregnancy.
10266.statement: Thinking that abortion is the only option following a positive genetic test result during pregnancy.
10266.correction: The lesson explores the various options and support that are available to parents who have a high probability of passing on alleles that can affect their child's health.

9374.belief: Small organisms and plants don't respire (only humans and other large animals).
9374.statement: That small organisms and plants don't respire (only humans and other large animals).
9374.correction: This lesson demonstrates experimentally that small organisms respire.

349.belief: Not appreciating that increasing temperature up to the optimum has a different effect on rate than increasing temperature above the optimum.
349.statement: Not appreciating that increasing temperature up to the optimum has a different effect on rate than increasing temperature above the optimum.
349.correction: The effects on rate of increasing temperature up to and beyond the optimum are explained.

9991.statement: Students often use the term "zoom in" instead of focus.
9991.correction: You must correct the term "zoom in" to focus. You are not making the image larger, you are focussing to make the image clearer.

5829.belief: The process of osmosis, the direction of movement from high to low water concentration, and the effect that this has on plant cells in terms of turgidity and flaccidity are frequently confused.
5829.statement: The process of osmosis, the direction of movement from high to low water concentration, and the effect that this has on plant cells in terms of turgidity and flaccidity are frequently confused.
5829.correction: Errors are explored, explained and questioned, and clear demonstrations of turgidity and flaccidity and the effects that these have on a plant are demonstrated. This will be reinforced by observation of these processes using a light microscope.

4567.belief: The menstrual cycle is not linked with reproduction; that hormones only control mood.
4567.statement: That the menstrual cycle is not linked with reproduction; that hormones only control mood.
4567.correction: Diagrams to show the clear effect of hormones on changes in the menstrual cycle and discuss the importance of the process to fertilisation.

3901.belief: IVF is highly effective without side effects. People can already choose the features of a baby. All people can have IVF from the NHS.
3901.statement: IVF is highly effective without side effects. People can already choose the features of a baby. All people can have IVF from the NHS.
3901.correction: IVF is less than 40% effective and this decreases with the age of the mother over 35. Genetic testing of embryos can be used to look for a disease, but genes cannot be altered. There is criteria for receiving IVF from the NHS and it is limited.

3185.belief: Fruit can only ripen whilst it is on the plant.
3185.statement: Fruit can only ripen whilst it is on the plant.
3185.correction: Discussion of fruits that are picked unripe, e.g. nectarines, tomatoes, avocados, bananas, and that they are ripened in transit.

6443.statement: Pupils are familiar with the physiological changes that occur in the body when they get cold or hot, but are unaware of the role of the brain in the detection and coordination of this response.
6443.correction: The role of the hypothalamus and thermoregulatory centre in this process are clearly explained and built into the process model of managing the familiar physiological responses.

10538.belief: Understanding how kidney filtration is controlled is complex, multifaceted and involves fairly obscure parts of the body so there is a lot of new content in this topic.
10538.statement: Understanding how kidney filtration is controlled is complex, multifaceted and involves fairly obscure parts of the body so there is a lot of new content in this topic.
10538.correction: The parts of the process are broken down into individual steps, introduced with care and supporting illustrations, checked, reviewed and backed up with reinforcing tasks.

4424.belief: Many pupils will believe that by halving the distance from a light source, the light intensity will double.
4424.statement: Many pupils will believe that by halving the distance from a light source, the light intensity will double.
4424.correction: As a result of light travelling in all directions, this aspect needs to be thought of in terms of area (two dimensions). The lesson takes pupils through an example which demonstrates how light intensity is proportional to the square of the distance.

2904.belief: Failing to realise that the plateau on a rate graph can occur because another factor (not named on the axes) has become limiting.
2904.statement: Failing to realise that the plateau on a rate graph can occur because another factor (not named on the axes) has become limiting.
2904.correction: The lesson explores rate graphs in which multiple limiting factors are affecting the rate of photosynthesis.

4714.belief: Monoclonal antibodies can act as a 'magic bullet' to deliver medication to certain cells.
4714.statement: Monoclonal antibodies can act as a 'magic bullet' to deliver medication to certain cells.
4714.correction: The human body is complex and therapies using monoclonal antibodies have had some serious side effects. New treatments should always be treated with caution.

10284.belief: An increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide will be beneficial by increasing photosynthesis and producing more food.
10284.statement: Thinking that an increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide will be beneficial by increasing photosynthesis and producing more food.
10284.correction: The lesson explores why the negative effects of increasing atmospheric carbon dioxide outweigh any benefits from increased rate of photosynthesis.
